written_by: Claude Code, for Ryan Saleh to check
notes: Biological sciences for Explore (spec 21), batch 2. Every name and description is in Stackd's own words; nothing is copied from UC's page. C-ID numbers, the template number and revision, the degree name, the unit totals and the campus major names are copied exactly. UC pathway: the Biological Sciences Transfer Pathway page on admission.universityofcalifornia.edu (it states no term or year; academic_year is the year it was checked). TMC: template #2014, the PDF in source_url. An option with no C-ID number has an empty c_id, which needs the migration 20261031120000_explore_option_no_c_id.sql before this file can be imported. Topics in both pathways (Counts for both): biology-sequence, chemistry-general. UC's calculus (a full year) and the template's calculus (the first course) are kept apart, like the physics split in Computer Science: calculus-single and calculus-first. The UC row says Cal State's degree asks for only the first course. Organic chemistry is UC only. Check every row against its source, delete each todo once confirmed, fill in retrieved_at on both pathways, then run: npm run import -- data/raw/explore/biological-sciences.json --dry-run

requirements.name: General chemistry with lab, a full year
requirements.description: The year-long chemistry series for science majors, with labs.

requirements.name: Calculus, a full year
requirements.description: Single-variable calculus for STEM majors. Finish the whole year-long sequence. Cal State's transfer degree asks for only the first course.

requirements.name: Organic chemistry with lab, a full year
requirements.description: The year-long organic chemistry series, with labs. Cal State's degree doesn't ask for it. UC says finishing it after transfer won't hurt your chances, and that some campuses also want calculus-based physics or a statistics course before you graduate.
